transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you that brought you in today?

Well, I guess it’s my eating that’s gotten strange. For months now it’s been all turned around. Some days I just sort of pick at toast and drink coffee, and then other days I find myself standing in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don’t even really want. I used to bake sometimes, actually—my mother had this lemon cake she made—but now it’s like I’m buying things and not even enjoying them. It just doesn’t feel like me.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or have lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yes… yes, I have. Most days I wake up and there’s just this heavy, sad feeling sitting on me. It’s there before I even get out of bed. I’ll go into the kitchen, and it’s bright in there in the morning, and I’ll make coffee like I always do, but it’s like… the warmth has gone out of everything.

I used to like little things like that, the smell of coffee, the light through the window—my neighbor has these red flowers outside I used to notice—but now it all feels kind of far away. I don’t know, it’s hard to explain. It’s just sad, most days.
Have you been feeling fatigued or lacking in energy most days, even when you haven’t done much physically?

Yes… I do. Even on nights when my aunt doesn’t call out and I actually get a full night, I still feel worn down by breakfast. It’s strange, because I’ll think, well, I slept, so I should be able to do normal things… but carrying laundry feels like too much, or making phone calls just drains me.

I used to be able to get those little things done without thinking. My aunt always says the phone is the easiest chore because you’re just sitting there, but it doesn’t feel that way lately. It takes more out of me than it should.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight over the past few months?

Yes… that’s actually one of the main reasons I came in. My eating’s been all turned around for months now. Some days I barely want anything, just toast and coffee, and then other days I’m in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don’t even really enjoy.

It’s odd because I used to like baking, like real baking, not just grabbing things in a store… but lately it’s more like I’m just doing it without feeling much about it. I can’t say exactly what my weight’s done, but the appetite part has definitely been different.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past few months?

I’m not exactly sure about the number on the scale… I haven’t been keeping track like I probably should. I used to weigh myself more, back when I was trying to be careful before my niece’s wedding—well, that was a whole thing with dresses and everybody fussing.

But I can tell my eating has been strange for months. That’s part of why I came in. Some days I just pick at toast and coffee, and then other days I’ll be standing in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don’t even really want. So… weight-wise, I don’t know exactly, but my appetite’s definitely been all over the place.
Have you been feeling like you’re not good enough or blamed yourself for things that aren’t entirely your fault?

I don’t know… not in a clear way, I guess. I mean, I do second-guess myself about little things, like whether I forgot something at the store or said something wrong on the phone, but I don’t know if that’s the same as what you mean.

My aunt will say, “Don’t make everything about you,” and then I start thinking maybe I am doing that, but then she says that about everyone, honestly. She even said it to the neighbor when his dog got loose, which was… I don’t know, kind of beside the point.

So… I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say I’m blaming myself for things that aren’t my fault, exactly.
Have you noticed any significant weight loss or gain recently, even if it’s just from changes in how much you’ve been eating?

I don’t really know the number, honestly. I haven’t been watching the scale. But… yes, the eating part has been really off for months now. That’s actually part of why I came in.

Some days I’ll just sort of pick at toast and coffee, and then other days I’m standing in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don’t even really enjoy. I used to actually like baking, you know, like making things from scratch, but this is different… it’s more like I’m just wandering around and putting things in the basket. So I can’t say for sure if I’ve gained or lost much, but my appetite has definitely changed.

Have you found yourself eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most people would eat in a similar period under similar circumstances, like finishing off a whole cake or a big bag of chips even when you're not hungry?

I don’t know if it’s like… finishing a whole cake, exactly. It’s more that my eating has gotten all turned around for months now. Some days I barely get through toast and coffee, and then other days I’m in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don’t even really enjoy.

It’s not even like when I used to bake for people—my neighbor loved those lemon bars, though she always said they were too sweet and then took three home. This is different. I’m just sort of there, putting things in the basket, and I don’t feel like I’m enjoying it much.
Have you found yourself eating, in a short amount of time, a large amount of food—like an entire cake or a big bag of snacks—even when you weren't really hungry?

Not like an entire cake, no… I don’t think so. It’s more that my eating’s just been all turned around for months. That’s part of why I came in.

Some days I’ll only pick at toast and coffee, and then other days I’m standing in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don’t even really enjoy. I used to know which cookies were worth getting, because my aunt was always picky about the coconut ones, but lately it’s not like that. I’m just sort of buying them, not really hungry exactly.
Would you say that most days, your mood is down or sad for most of the day, even in the absence of specific stressors?

Yes… most days, I think so. I wake up and it’s like there’s this heavy, sad feeling already sitting on me before I’ve even done anything.

And it’s strange because my kitchen gets nice light in the morning, and I’ll have the coffee going, and it should feel warm or normal, but it doesn’t. It’s like the warmth has gone out of everything. Even when there isn’t some particular reason that day, it’s just… there.

When you’ve had days where you’re not eating much—like just toast and coffee—does that feel like a loss of appetite, or is it more that you’re not interested in eating, even though you might still feel hungry?

It’s… more like I just don’t have any interest in it. I mean, I came in because my eating’s been so turned around for months now. Some days I’m just picking at toast and coffee, and then other days I’m in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don’t even really enjoy.

I used to like going to bakeries, actually—there was one with these little almond cookies my mother liked—but now it’s not really about wanting food. It’s just off. Like my body and my head aren’t matching up.
Have you noticed any clear changes in your weight recently, such as weight loss or weight gain, even if it’s just from the changes in your eating habits?

I haven’t really been tracking the number, honestly. I mean, my clothes… sometimes I think they fit a little different, but I don’t know.

What I do know is my eating’s been all turned around for months now. Some days I’m just picking at toast and coffee, and then other days I’ll end up standing in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don’t even really enjoy. I used to always compare prices on those little cookies—my aunt had opinions about the coconut ones—but now I’m just sort of there, putting things in the basket. So… weight, I’m not sure, but the eating has definitely changed.
Have you noticed that you don’t take pleasure in or aren’t interested in doing activities or hobbies that you used to enjoy, outside of eating or baking?

Yes… yes, I have. I used to get really excited about quilting squares, picking out the fabrics and laying them all out on the table. I’d spend ages matching colors—my neighbor used to say I had “too many blues,” which I probably did.

And bowling night, too. I used to look forward to that, and planning potlucks from the church calendar, seeing who was bringing what. Now I’ll look at my sewing things or I’ll see something posted for church, and I just… can’t make myself care about it the way I used to. It’s like I know I used to enjoy it, but I can’t reach that feeling.
Even though you’re not sure about the exact number, have you noticed your clothes feeling looser or tighter than before, or do you think you’ve lost or gained weight recently?

I don’t know if I could say looser or tighter exactly… I haven’t been paying close attention like that. I came in more because the eating itself has been so turned around for months.

Some days I’m barely picking at toast and coffee, and then other days I’ll find myself in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don’t even really enjoy. I’ll be looking at the frosting colors or remembering how my mother used to pick through day-old rolls, and then I realize I’m just standing there with things in my basket. So… weight, I’m not sure. The eating has definitely changed, though.
Even if it’s just from looking in the mirror or how your clothes fit, have you noticed yourself looking thinner or losing weight recently?

I can’t really say I look thinner, no… I haven’t been standing in front of the mirror much. I know you asked that already, I’m sorry — I just don’t have a good answer on the weight part.

What I came in because of is more the eating. It’s been all turned around for months now. Some days it’s just toast and coffee, picking at it like it’s a chore, and then other days I’m in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don’t even really like. I’ll look at the little cakes, or the cookies, and think about how I used to compare prices, and then suddenly they’re in my basket. So… I don’t know about thinner, but my eating’s definitely not like it used to be.
When you find yourself buying sweets in the bakery aisle or eating more than usual, do you feel like you can’t control it—like you’re not really choosing to do it, but it just happens?

I don’t know if it feels like “can’t control it” exactly… I wouldn’t put it that strongly. It’s more like my eating’s been all turned around for months now.

Some days I just pick at toast and coffee, like even that feels like too much bother, and then other days I’ll be standing in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don’t even really enjoy. I’ll look at the little frosted ones, and it reminds me of when we’d get day-old things after church, and then I realize I’ve put them in the basket. So… I guess it sort of happens, but I’m not sure I’d say I’m not choosing it. It’s just not like me.
Have you found that you don’t look forward to or enjoy things the way you used to, even things that weren’t about food or baking?

Yes… I think so. I used to really look forward to things, like picking out quilting squares — the colors and little patterns, you know, getting them lined up just right. And bowling night, even if I wasn’t any good, I liked seeing everyone.

Now I’ll look at my fabric or see something on the church calendar, like a potluck coming up, and I just… I can’t make myself care the way I used to. I’ll think, “I should plan something, I should go,” but it feels flat. Like it’s happening on the other side of a window.
